projects_1.title:
Cohabitation timing &
adolescent childbearing
projects_1.description:
“Cohabitation timing and childbearing or current pregnancy among married adolescents in Bangladesh: a complex-survey analysis of the 2022 BDHS.”

Complex-survey analysis of the association between cohabitation timing and childbearing or current pregnancy among married adolescents in Bangladesh, using the 2022 BDHS. The study accounts for the survey sampling design and examines associations rather than causal effects.
projects_1.tags: Complex surveys, Logistic regression, Reproductive health
projects_1.note:
Authors: Md Ikramul Haq Khan, Israt Jahan, Mohammad Amirul Islam, Rohan Dalpatadu, Mohammad Karim.
Version 3 posted October 11, 2026 · medRxiv preprint · Not peer reviewed.
This research was presented at the ASA Nevada Chapter Fall Symposium, UNLV, October 10, 2026, under its earlier presentation title.
Weighting clarification revised October 15, 2026; website manuscript available alongside the October 11 version. The new revision has not been uploaded to medRxiv.

projects_1.title:
Statistical approaches
to epidemic modeling
projects_1.description:
Developing a thesis direction around epidemic models, stochastic components, and the estimation of infection-rate behavior.

Areas being explored include simulation, distributional assumptions, model comparison, and uncertainty assessment. The research question and analysis plan are being refined.
projects_1.note:
Chair: Prof. Rohan Dalpatadu
Co-advisor: Dr. Miguel Fudolig
Current priority: define one thesis question and a baseline simulation with advisor input. Target: JSM 2027 as an alternative to the BDHS contraception project, subject to readiness.

projects_1.title: Evaluating AI-generated regression analyses
projects_1.description: Developing a study of whether AI systems produce statistically defensible biomedical regression analyses. Current work focuses on reviewing existing evaluation tasks and designing a bounded simulation pilot. Novelty and feasibility remain under review.
projects_1.note: Planned target: SIAM Conference on Mathematics of Data Science, future edition/call to be confirmed. MDS26 submissions are closed. Detailed unpublished protocols remain private; no benchmark results or acceptance are claimed.

projects_1.title: Contraceptive continuity after method discontinuation
projects_1.description: A BDHS 2022 calendar-based study of switching, subsequent nonuse and recorded pregnancy after selected contraceptive discontinuations. The analysis combines complex-survey estimation, sensitivity to population definitions, and grouped model validation.
projects_1.tags: Complex surveys, Reproductive health, Model validation
projects_1.note: Planned: BDHS contraception poster at the 4th Annual Wine and Research Evening, November 12, 2026 (subject to acceptance); also a candidate topic for JSM 2027, alongside epidemic modeling. Separate from the adolescent-childbearing preprint. Independent review remains outstanding.

projects_2.title: Food safety practices in cereal-based manufacturing
projects_2.description: Assessment of food safety control systems in small- and medium-scale manufacturing establishments, focusing on hygiene, regulatory compliance, and operational performance.

projects_2.title: Statistical analysis of cyberbullying
projects_2.description: Survey-based research on cyberbullying among youth, examining gender differences, psychological impacts, social-media involvement, and parental and institutional responses.
